content:
# Sirach 39 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** SIR 039 | **Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Total Disagreements:** 17

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "seek out the wisdom" vs. "seek the wisdom"

- **EMET:** "will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients"
- **LOGOS:** "will seek the wisdom of all the ancients"
- **PNEUMA:** "searches out the wisdom of every ancient generation"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "will seek the wisdom of all the ancients" — LOGOS; "seek out" (EMET) is acceptable but slightly redundant; PNEUMA's "every ancient generation" interprets "all the ancients" too expansively.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "discourse of notable men" vs. "discourse of famous men"

- **EMET:** "the discourse of notable men"
- **LOGOS:** "the discourse of famous men"
- **PNEUMA:** "the teachings of great thinkers"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the discourses of famous men" — ἐνδόξων ἀνδρῶν; "famous" (LOGOS) is most literal; "notable" (EMET) is acceptable; PNEUMA's "great thinkers" adds interpretive content.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.2b: "subtleties of parables" vs. "subtleties of figures of speech"

- **EMET:** "subtleties of parables"
- **LOGOS:** "subtleties of figures of speech"
- **PNEUMA:** "deeper meanings of figurative speech"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "subtleties of figures of speech" — παραβολῶν can mean "parables" or "comparisons/figures"; "figures of speech" (LOGOS) is broader and more accurate here.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.4: "lands of foreign nations" vs. "lands of foreign peoples"

- **EMET:** "lands of foreign nations"
- **LOGOS:** "lands of foreign peoples"
- **PNEUMA:** "foreign lands"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "lands of foreign peoples" (LOGOS) — more precise than "nations"; PNEUMA's compression loses the specificity.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.4b: "tests the good and evil among men" vs. "tests what is good and evil in human experience"

- **EMET:** "he tests the good and the evil among men"
- **LOGOS:** "he tests what is good and evil in human experience"
- **PNEUMA:** "learning first-hand what is good and what is harmful"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "he tests the good and the evil in human experience" — combines; "experience" (LOGOS) provides the contextual frame; PNEUMA's "harmful" for "evil" is too restrictive.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.6: "spirit of understanding" vs. "spirit of discernment"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "spirit of understanding"
- **PNEUMA:** "spirit of discernment"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "spirit of understanding" — πνεῦμα συνέσεως; "understanding" is the standard translation for σύνεσις in LXX contexts.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.7: "meditate on his secrets" vs. "meditate on the Lord's mysteries"

- **EMET:** "meditate on his secrets"
- **LOGOS:** "meditate on the Lord's mysteries"
- **PNEUMA:** "meditate on God's hidden purposes"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "meditate on his secrets" — EMET; ἀποκρύφων is "hidden things/secrets"; "mysteries" (LOGOS) has a technical religious connotation that is secondary; "purposes" (PNEUMA) is too interpretive.

---

## Disagreement 8 — v.9: "blotted out" vs. "erased"

- **EMET:** "it will never be blotted out"
- **LOGOS:** "it will never be erased"
- **PNEUMA:** "it will never be forgotten"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "it will never be blotted out" — EMET; the image of ink being wiped from a scroll is vivid and should be kept; "forgotten" (PNEUMA) is too ordinary.

---

## Disagreement 9 — v.11: "goes to rest" vs. "enters into rest" vs. "dies"

- **EMET:** "if he goes to rest"
- **LOGOS:** "if he enters into rest"
- **PNEUMA:** "if he dies, he goes content"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "if he goes to his rest" — the euphemism κοιμηθῇ ("falls asleep") should be preserved as a dignified biblical expression; PNEUMA's "goes content" adds an emotional gloss.

---

## Disagreement 10 — v.12: moon simile

- **EMET:** "I am filled like the moon at the full"
- **LOGOS:** "I am as full as the moon at its full"
- **PNEUMA:** "I'm filled to the brim like the full moon"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "I am as full as the moon at the full" — LOGOS; the repetition "full...at the full" echoes the Greek; PNEUMA's "brim" adds a liquid metaphor not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 11 — v.13: "holy children" vs. "people of God"

- **EMET:** "Listen to me, you holy children"
- **LOGOS:** "Listen to me, O holy children"
- **PNEUMA:** "Listen to me, you people of God!"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Listen to me, O holy children" — LOGOS; τέκνα ὅσια is the literal form; PNEUMA's "people of God" is a free interpretation.

---

## Disagreement 12 — v.14: "scatter your fragrance" vs. "spread your fragrance"

- **EMET:** "Scatter your fragrance and sing a hymn of praise"
- **LOGOS:** "Let your voice carry sweetness and bless the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "Lift your voices and sing; bless the Lord"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Scatter your fragrance and sing a hymn of praise" — EMET; the fragrance and singing are two separate imperatives; LOGOS appears to merge them.

---

## Disagreement 13 — v.16: "All the works of the Lord are very good"

- All three agree on this core verse; minor differences only.
- **PNEUMA** adds "Every" for the second clause; EMET/LOGOS use "whatever."
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "All the works of the Lord are very good, and whatever he commands will be done in its time" — follows EMET/LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 14 — v.17: "stood in a heap" — water image

- All three preserve this; LOGOS notes "Nile" in v.22.
- **EMET:** "the waters stood in a heap"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** same.
- Minor: "reservoirs of water" vs. "great reservoirs" (PNEUMA).
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the waters stood in a heap, and the reservoirs of water" — follows EMET/LOGOS without PNEUMA's embellishment.

---

## Disagreement 15 — v.22: flood-river simile

- **EMET:** "like a river...like a flood"
- **LOGOS:** "like a river...floods it like the Nile"
- **PNEUMA:** "flows over...like a river...like a flood"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "like a river and saturates it like a flood" — EMET; LOGOS's "Nile" adds a specific geographical reference that may be a secondary reading.

---

## Disagreement 16 — v.26: list of necessities

- All three give the same list; differ slightly in arrangement.
- **EMET:** "wheat flour and milk and honey, the blood of the grape and oil"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "milk and honey, the juice of the grape"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the juice of the grape" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; "juice" is cleaner than EMET's "blood."

---

## Disagreement 17 — v.28: "move mountains" vs. "uproot mountains" vs. "flatten mountains"

- **EMET:** "they can move mountains"
- **LOGOS:** "they can uproot mountains"
- **PNEUMA:** "they can flatten mountains"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "they can move mountains" — κινήσουσιν ὄρη; "move" is the standard translation and carries a resonance with the NT's "faith to move mountains"; "uproot" (LOGOS) and "flatten" (PNEUMA) are both plausible but secondary.
